candidate.answerReason: Driving took 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 hours, leaving 0.5 hour, or 30 minutes, for lunch.

methods.label: Find the driving time first
methods.explanation:
The total trip time consists of driving and lunch, so first find how much time Casey spent driving. Average driving speed equals distance divided by driving time, giving
\[
\text{driving time}=\frac{100}{40}=2.5\text{ hours}.
\]
Lunch was her only stop, so the lunch break lasted \(3-2.5=0.5\) hour. Since one hour contains \(60\) minutes, this is
\[
0.5\times60=\boxed{30\text{ minutes}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses the elementary distance-speed-time relationship, subtraction, and conversion between hours and minutes.
